answer.rationale: Expiry in 14 days with no auto-renew, 94% line load, and no buffer makes continuity binding: a primary gap would hit assembly immediately. Switching to the low-cost vendor would meet the 18% spend cut on price alone and memory_c2 reports a prior switch cut unit cost with fast onboarding and clean invoicing, but that does not establish that a full primary cutover is low-risk under today’s zero-buffer conditions, so switch is not chosen yet. memory_c1 indicates incumbent renewal preserved integration and deliveries; memory_c4 indicates renewal-time market benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms; memory_c6 indicates a longer commitment can cut unit cost without shrinking scope. Intended action is therefore to negotiate the expiring primary against the competitive quote (and term length) rather than switch, blindly renew, or add a source. memory_c5’s deferral applied to a non-critical month-to-month service and does not transfer; memory_c3’s second source does not replace the expiring primary and would consume the single decision slot. Unverified: whether prior negotiation moved price enough to approach 18%, and whether last year’s low-cost onboarding hid delivery or quality caveats. Flagging downstream production-value risk until those records are checked.
